page: Amazon Web Services c5a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor. This x86_64 architecture instance features 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and includes a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks indicate average capabilities across standard workloads. The server achieves average scores in Geekbench single-core, multi-core, software compilation, and ray tracing tests. Passmark CPU, memory, and database operations also fall within the average range. However, raw compute benchmarks show some limitations, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring in the bottom 10% and multi-core performance in the bottom 25%. Uncached memory bandwidth read and write tests also rank in the bottom 25%, though cached small-block reads remain average.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c5a.2xlarge offers a balanced compute-to-memory ratio for workloads that do not require high-speed local storage or massive memory footprints. It is suitable for tasks such as static web serving, software compilation, and light text or image processing. It can also handle small-scale language model inference, though performance drops significantly on larger models.
description: Amazon Web Services c5a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of DDR4 RAM. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor running at 3.3 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor, this x86_64 server delivers a balanced 2.0 GB of memory per core. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs, relying on a 2 Gbps baseline network connection. Benchmark data positions the c5a.2xlarge in the average tier for software compilation, ray tracing, and database operations, though it exhibits weaker performance in raw stress-ng CPU tests and uncached memory bandwidth. This instance is best suited for general compute tasks, static web serving, and moderate processing workloads that do not demand high-speed local storage.
